card.name: Words inside reasoning clauses
card.fires_on: Short function-like words right after a reason or contrast is set up, such as 'because', 'and there', or 'anyway'. The marked word sits just before the claim is stated.

modes.label: After 'because' or 'there'
modes.description: A verb or contraction right after 'because' or 'there' that begins the stated reason.
modes.example: and there<<’s>> no manufacturing, packaging or shipping involved.

modes.label: Discourse 'anyway'
modes.description: The word 'anyway' or the comma after it, used as an aside before a point.
modes.example: And,<< anyway>>, hope still remains of avoiding the meltdown

modes.label: Verb in a warning rationale
modes.description: A verb in a label sentence explaining why a caution applies.
modes.example: WARNINGS Because rare instances of anaphylactoid reactions have<< occurred>> in patients receiving parenteral corticoster
